semantic_fragments.content: The tests results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. This report shall not be reproduced except in full without the written approval of the testing laboratory. List of test equipment must be kept on file and available for review. Additional test data and/or information provided in the attachments to this report. Throughout this report a comma/point is used as the decimal separator.

This product is a high-tech infra-red (IR) thermometer designed to take human body temperature by measuring the energy of IR emitted from the forehead. The product will help you to assess you and your family members' health conditions easily and quickly.

Possible test case verdicts: N/A - test case does not apply to the test object; Pass (P) - test object does meet the requirement; N/E - test object was not evaluated for the requirement; Fail (F) - test object does not meet the requirement. Abbreviations: N.C. = normal condition; S.F.C. = single fault condition; MOOP = means of Operator protection; MOPP = means of Patient protection.
Test laboratory: Tianxu(Tianjin)Testing Technology Service Co.,LTD, Address: 101, First floor, Building L, No.3 JinPing Street, Ya An Road, Nankai District, Tianjin, China.
The test results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. Without permission of the Report department this test report is not permitted to be duplicated in extracts.

Insulation diagram is a graphical representation of equipment insulation barriers, protective impedance and protective earthing. Conventions: All isolation barriers are identified by letters between separate parts of diagram, for example separate transformer windings, optocouplers, wire insulation, creepage and clearance distances. Parts connected to earth with large dots are protectively earthed. Other connections to earth are functional. Applied parts are extended beyond the equipment enclosure and terminated with an arrow. Parts accessible to the operator only are extended outside of the enclosure, but are not terminated with an arrow.

A measured value must be provided in the value columns for the device under evaluation. The symbol > (greater than sign) must not be used. Switch-mode power supplies must be re-evaluated in the device under evaluation therefore N/A must not be used with a generic statement that the component is certified.
EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE stated in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE as 5 years. This is per Clause 4.4 of IEC60601-1.

No alternative means of addressing particular RISKS were provided or used. Per Clause 4.5, alternative means must be justified by the MANUFACTURER showing RESIDUAL RISKS are comparable to those resulting from standard requirements, based on scientific data, clinical opinion, or comparative studies.

No COMPONENT WITH HIGH-INTEGRITY CHARACTERISTICS was used in this ME EQUIPMENT per Clause 4.9. No evaluation of such components for conditions of use and reasonably foreseeable misuse during EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE was required.

All components and wiring are used within their specified ratings. Reliability of components used as MEANS OF PROTECTION was assessed for conditions of use in ME EQUIPMENT. Components complied with applicable safety requirements of relevant IEC or ISO standards (see appended table 8.10).

Environmental test conditions: Temperature 10℃-40℃; Relative Humidity 15%RH-95%RH; Atmospheric Pressure 700hPa-1060hPa. Test lab environment under controlled conditions. Test results of excessive temperature were adjusted to ambient temperature 40℃.
Device is powered by an INTERNAL ELECTRICAL POWER SOURCE only (not connected to SUPPLY MAINS). All clauses related to SUPPLY MAINS connection (4.10.2, 4.11, 5.5) are marked N/A.

For Clause 5.7: ME EQUIPMENT heated to a temperature between T and T+4°C for at least 4 hours and placed in a humidity chamber (relative humidity 93%±3%) with an ambient within 2°C of T in the range of +20°C to +32°C for 48 hours for units rated IPX0. For units rated higher than IPX0, test time extended to 168 hours. Manually detachable parts removed and treated concurrently with major parts; manually removable ACCESS COVERS opened and detached.
Clause 5.8: Unless stated otherwise, tests in this standard are sequenced as in Annex B to prevent influencing results of any subsequent test.

Clause 5.9.2.1: Accessibility, when necessary, determined using standard test finger of Fig 6 applied in a bent or straight position. Openings preventing entry of test finger of Fig. 6 mechanically tested with a straight un-jointed test finger of the same dimensions with a force of 30 N. When the straight un-jointed test finger entered, test with the standard test finger (Fig 6) was repeated, if necessary, by pushing the finger through the opening. Result: No opening found.

Clause 5.9.2.3: Conductive parts of actuating mechanisms of electrical controls accessible after removal of handles, knobs, levers and the like are regarded as ACCESSIBLE PARTS. However, conductive parts of actuating mechanisms are not considered ACCESSIBLE PARTS when removal of handles, knobs, etc. required the use of a TOOL. Result: No such conductive part found.

Clause 6.2: EQUIPMENT with means of connection to a SUPPLY MAINS complied with CLASS I or CLASS II ME EQUIPMENT requirements when so connected, and when not connected to SUPPLY MAINS complied with INTERNALLY POWERED ME EQUIPMENT requirements.

Clause 7.1.3: Required markings can be removed only with a TOOL or by appreciable force, are durable and remain CLEARLY LEGIBLE during EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE of ME EQUIPMENT in NORMAL USE. Test result: Can be removed only with appreciable force.

At least markings in 7.2.2, 7.2.5, 7.2.6 (not for PERMANENTLY INSTALLED ME EQUIPMENT), 7.2.10, and 7.2.13 were applied when size of EQUIPMENT, its part, an ACCESSORY, or ENCLOSURE did not permit application of all required markings. Remaining markings fully recorded in ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTS (Operation guide).

Software forming part of a PEMS must be identified with a unique identifier, such as revision level or date of release/issue, and identification must be available to designated persons. (Clause 7.2.2, Verdict: P)

ME EQUIPMENT intended to receive power from other electrical equipment in an ME SYSTEM where compliance with this standard is dependent on that other equipment must have one of the following: (1) the name or trademark of the manufacturer of the other electrical equipment and type reference marked adjacent to the relevant connection point; or (2) SAFETY SIGN ISO 7010-M002 adjacent to the relevant connection point with listing of required details in the instructions for use; or (3) a special connector style not commonly available on the market with listing of required details in the instructions for use. All items marked N/A for this product.

Connection to the Supply Mains (Clause 7.2.6): All sub-requirements including rated supply voltage marking, supply voltage range, nature of supply, type of current, symbols from Table D.1 (IEC 60417-5032, 5032-1, 5032-2, 5031, 5033), and rated supply frequency are all marked N/A for this product.

The ME EQUIPMENT is classified as IP22 per IEC 60529, uses TYPE BF APPLIED PARTS with Symbol 20 (IEC 60417-5333), is intended for CONTINUOUS OPERATION, has no accessible fuse-holder, no high voltage terminal devices, no special cooling provisions, no socket-outlets, no type B or type CF applied parts, no defibrillation-proof applied parts, and no special packaging instructions. Limited mechanical stability is addressed in clause 9.4.
The device under test (PT9L) is PORTABLE equipment, not MOBILE ME EQUIPMENT, therefore marking requirements for SAFE WORKING LOAD in kilograms per clause 7.2.21 are not applicable.

The device PT9L does not use lithium batteries or fuel cells; therefore all related requirements for warning markings, risk management file assessment, and accompanying documents warnings regarding hazardous situations from incorrect battery replacement are not applicable.

The device PT9L does not have a protective earth terminal, functional earth terminal, or terminals for supply conductors. Therefore, clauses 7.3.5, 7.3.6, and 7.3.7 related marking requirements are not applicable.

Clause 7.4.1 details requirements for power control switches on ME EQUIPMENT: mains switches and switches controlling power to ME EQUIPMENT must clearly indicate 'on' and 'off' positions via IEC symbols (5007/5008), adjacent indicator lights, or other unambiguous means. Switches for parts of equipment may additionally use IEC 60417-5264/5265. Stand-by switches may use IEC 60417-5009. Bistable push buttons must use IEC 60417-5010 with status indication. Momentary-on push buttons must use IEC 60417-5011 or equivalent status indication. All sub-clauses under 7.4.1 are marked N/A for this device.

Clause 7.5 SAFETY SIGNS requirements: The risk management process must identify markings used to convey warnings, prohibitions, or mandatory actions that mitigate risks not obvious to the operator (per ISO 14971). ISO 7010-M002 symbol is provided to indicate following the instruction for use. Safety signs must use colours per ISO 3864-1, include appropriate precautions or instructions to reduce risks, and be described in the instructions for use in a language acceptable to the intended operator. All 7.5 requirements pass (verdict P).

Indicator lights color coding requirements: Red indicator lights mean Warning (immediate response by OPERATOR required); Yellow indicator lights mean Caution (prompt response by OPERATOR required); Green indicator lights mean Ready for use. Red used only for emergency control.

Instructions for use when PATIENT is an intended OPERATOR must include: statement that the PATIENT is an intended OPERATOR; warning against servicing and maintenance while the ME EQUIPMENT is in use; functions the PATIENT can safely use and which functions the PATIENT cannot safely use; maintenance the PATIENT can perform.

The device PT9L has no protective earth conductor, is not Class I equipment, and accompanying documents are provided on paper rather than electronically. Several clauses related to protective earth conductors and power supply cord colors are marked N/A.

Multiple clauses of IEC60601-1 section 7.9.2 are evaluated for compliance. Requirements cover labeling and instructions for use including: electromagnetic interference warnings, battery management, power source specifications, equipment description and functions, operator/patient positioning, installation guidance, operational instructions, controls/displays/signals explanation, error/fault messages, operation termination, cleaning/disinfection/sterilization, and maintenance procedures. References are consistently made to the Operation Guide sections: 'NOTICE', 'SETUP AND OPERATING PROCEDURES', 'MAINTENANCE', and 'Product errors and troubleshooting'.

Varnishing, enamelling, oxidation, and similar protective finishes and coatings with sealing compounds re-plasticizing at temperatures expected during operation and sterilization are disregarded as MEANS OF PROTECTION. Components and wiring forming a MEANS OF PROTECTION must comply with 8.10. Insulation, CREEPAGE, CLEARANCES, components or earth connections not complying with 8.5.1.2 and 8.5.1.3 are not considered as MEANS OF PROTECTION, and failure of these parts is regarded as NORMAL CONDITION.

MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION (MOPP) requirements under 8.5.1.2: Solid insulation forming a MOPP must comply with dielectric strength test of Clause 8.8 at the test voltage specified in Table 6. A Y (Y1 or Y2) capacitor complying with IEC 60384-14 is considered one MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION. A single Y1 capacitor may be used for two MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION when the working voltage is less than 42.4 V peak a.c. or 60 V d.c.
